ops.title: Broker→daemon direction has no peer verification (confused-deputy)
ops.body:
Trust across the FuseKit broker↔daemon boundary is asymmetric, and the unverified direction is exploitable by any same-UID process.

**What is verified.** The Go holder authenticates the broker *inbound*: `internal/trust` (LOCAL_PEERCRED + LOCAL_PEERTOKEN + `csops_audittoken`), applied via `holder/trust.go` and `holder/runtime.go:652-665`. Separately, `daemonkit.ServingSigned` as `Cmd.Exec` verifies a spawned child's kernel-held code identity before release — a *spawn-time* check that does not apply to a launch that never goes through daemonkit's Spawn (e.g. `open -a CCPoolStatus --args ...`).

**What is not.** Nothing authenticates the daemon *from the broker's side*, ever. `Sources/DaemonKit/` (the Swift half) has zero `SecCode`/`LOCAL_PEERCRED` usage — the primitive is Go-only. So the broker will talk to whatever is listening at the path it was given.

**Why it matters.** `CatalogBrokerState.runBroker` (fusekit `Sources/FuseKit/Broker.swift:127`) polls the far end and executes whatever commands come back via `CatalogDomainController.execute`, posting results. An attacker-controlled listener does not merely receive data from the entitled broker — it *drives* it, with App Group entitlements the attacker's own process lacks.

**Why 0700 does not save it.** The socket's parent dir being 0700 blocks other UIDs, not other same-UID processes — which is exactly the confused-deputy attacker population. A same-UID process can bind the real path before the daemon starts (boot-order TOCTOU) and win the race.

**The path-equality fence is not a fix.** `Broker.swift:106` compares the argv socket path against an independently-derived Swift constant. That defends against *redirection* while leaving *impersonation* open, and it is what broke availability: the constant (`cc-pool` `widget/Sources/FileProviderRuntime/Configuration.swift` `holderSocketPath` = `~/.cc-pool/fusekit/fusekit.sock`) drifted from the live socket during the daemonkit v0.21.3 migration.

**Durable conclusion, independent of which remediation lands:** the real defect is not "wrong path" but "nothing on the client side ever checks who is listening." A correct fix either eliminates the dialed path entirely (pre-connected conns) or verifies the listener's code identity by audit token — never a path constant, prefix or exact.

Security review by gpt-5.6-sol via codex, 2026-08-16; both load-bearing claims independently verified against the source.
